issues.description: Master sets global base to the Windows-style path \CSTV_GroupAudits. A Linux working copy needs a relative project-root base with Stata started from the directory containing code/ and data/.

Master calls code/9_Append_Data Selection.do and code/Subsidiary_Data.do, but the supplied programs are code/9_Append_DataSelection.do and code/10_Subsidiary_Data.do. The final roster read also uses Identifier_Final Sample.dta while the package contains Identifiers_Final Samples.dta.

Code 3 imports Audit_Fee.xlsx although the package supplies Audit_Fee_2006-2013.xlsx; code 4 saves/reads annual Audit_FeeYYYY files under data/ for 2004-2005 but reads 2006-2013 files relative to base while code 3 saves them under data/.
Stage 6 writes the 2011 merged-price output to data2011... without the directory separator; stage 8 reads every PriceYYYY.dta relative to base although stage 7 saves them under data/.

Stage 6 reads 2015 down to 2000 SPPR_Financial_Audit files; stage 4 produces only 2004-2013. The 2000-2003 and 2014-2015 intermediates have no producer in the supplied master chain. Preserve the calls and annual branches pending the intended producer/source contract.

Stage 5 keys price rows from grouptcode/ltdmo, stage 6 creates a company-month key from financial groupcoycode/month, and stage 7/8 similarly join grouptcode to groupcoycode. The separate raw workbooks are absent, so the key-value and month alignment are not verified.

The packaged Subsidiaries.dta probe lists ASX_CODE and YEAR but no groupcoycode. Code 10 renames those to asxcode and year_SPPR, then merges using groupcoycode/year_SPPR. A historically valid company-key mapping and uniqueness contract is needed; do not substitute ASX code without support.

Code 13 reads AccountsPayable.dta without a supplied producer. It uses value349, value301 and value2600 with lags and groupcoycode/year_SPPR; these fields may be derivable from the already-required Aspect panel, so no independent raw-source requirement is assumed.

The supplied generic SUBS/ISO workbook has the expected headers and may support the source-specified distance/RL mapping, including New Caledonia mapped to FRA; its rows and full target coverage were not value-checked. Code 14 explicitly says GDP availability differs for territories/special administrative regions and expects a separate _GDP map, which is not established by the generic workbook.
